# reqlint — requirement wording checker (SYS 5100)

`reqlint` reads requirement statements and flags wording that often hides a problem: vague
terms, combinators, passive voice without an agent, escape clauses, open-ended lists, missing
units or tolerances, solution-in-disguise, pronouns, negatives, ambiguous time words, and more
(27 rules). It is used in the **Week 4 AI-drafted requirements audit (Lab 4)** and by
`sysml-kit lint`.

The rules are *inspired by* the characteristics of well-formed requirements described in the
INCOSE *Guide to Writing Requirements* (GtWR). Each rule carries a characteristic label
(e.g. *Unambiguous*, *Singular*, *Verifiable*) and a short explanation written by the course
team. **No GtWR text is reproduced**; read the Guide itself for the full rules.

> A clean run does not make a requirement good. `reqlint` checks wording only. It cannot tell
> whether a requirement is necessary, correct, feasible, traced to real evidence, or whose
> voice it carries. That judgement is the point of the lab.

## Install

```bash
pip install -e tools/reqlint          # from the course repository (Python 3.10+, no dependencies)
python -m reqlint --version           # works without installing, from the reqlint folder
```

## Use

```text
reqlint [options] FILE [FILE ...]
reqlint --text "The robot shall stop within 1.5 m." [--id REQ-04]
reqlint --list-rules [--format json] [--lang fr]
```

| Input | Format |
|---|---|
| `.csv` | header row with `id`, `text` (or `requirement`), optional `rationale`, `verification` |
| `.md` | Markdown tables with the same headers, or list items `- REQ-04: The robot shall ...` |
| `.sysml` | SysML v2 text: requirement ids `<'REQ-04'>` and the first `doc /* ... */` in each requirement |
| `.txt` | one requirement per line, `ID: text` |

Options: `--format text|json` · `--min-severity info|warning|error` (hide below) ·
`--fail-on error|warning|never` (default `error`) · `--rules RL-A,RL-B` · `--ignore RL-X` ·
`--glossary FILE` (one defined abbreviation per line; silences RL-ABBR for those) ·
`--lang fr` (French rule titles: stub, awaiting review).

**Exit codes:** `0` no finding at or above `--fail-on`; `1` at least one; `2` usage or input error.

**RL-RATIONALE / RL-VERIF** only fire when the input has a rationale / verification column
(CSV, Markdown table) and the cell is empty or the method is not one of Test, Analysis,
Inspection, Demonstration (ECSS also lists Review of design).

## Python API

```python
from reqlint import lint_text, load, lint_requirements, RULES
[f.rule for f in lint_text("The robot shall be able to stop quickly.")]   # ['RL-INFIN', 'RL-TIME']
findings = lint_requirements(load("model/robot.sysml"))
```

## Lab 4 materials

- `samples/week4_ai_drafted_requirements.csv` — 30 requirements written to imitate typical AI
  drafts across S1–S4 (two are well-formed controls: AI-08, AI-23).
- `samples/week4_key.json` — instructor key data (planted wording flaws, human-only flaws, example rewrites).
- `samples/week4_instructor_key.md` — rendered key, regenerated by `python samples/build_key.py`
  (a test fails if it is stale). Keep it out of student repositories.

## Tests

```bash
cd tools/reqlint && python -m pytest -q
```
